data.name: Plight
data.detailed_description:
RoGlass - A Roguelike Puzzle Game

Check out a new roguelike puzzle game by the designer of Plight!


Acerca do jogo

Delve into the immersive world of Plight, where darkness has consumed the planet, and its up to you to re-energize it! Challenge yourself with over 90 handcrafted levels that put your puzzle solving skills to the test!

Journey through the three expansive areas that make up the world of Plight. Learn how to manipulate the energy pylons scattered throughout the land and charge the main power pylons for each level. Use beam, creation, refractor, splitter, teleport pylons and more, to bring the planet back to life!

Features:
-3 unique areas
-90 handcrafted levels
-9 hidden secret levels
-A rating system that challenges you
(Prove your skill by obtaining all of the elusive green stars!)
-Immersive environments
-New challenges at every turn

reviews.review:
This is an interesting game, and its free!

You are a cyborg and your goal is to lit the final pylon in the game. How you do that is determined by the level itself, which will produce a puzzle for you to solve.

The puzzles start simple, and gradually get bigger. They're fun to solve.

The controls are a different story. The game lets you do most with the keyboard, but unfortunately not everything. You can play the game entirely with mouse, but that is even harder. The controls themselves are not all too bad, but in order to unlock the green stars, you need to get through a level as quickly as you can, and this is where the controls get in the way.

Also, in some levels where you rotate the pilons to redirect the laserbeams, although the controls try to snap the rotation, when redirection is involved, sometimes it is really taking 20 tries to get it just right. A button to slowly rotate the pylon is very welcome here.

It can be that you figured out the optimal route to get the puzzle solved as quickly as possible, but in your execution make a movement mistake (get stuck behind a wall, you click a pylon, but it doesn't get focus, you need to drag an game element, but you are just not that fast and precise with the mouse, etc) they are small agonies that made me decide to not go for green stars. I'll just solve the puzzles and that's it.

The game does have additional bonus items spread throughout the levels, and getting these are more challenging. They're great puzzles that will unlock a far more difficult puzzle. The concept is quite similar to The Talos Principle's bonus system of getting stars and unlocking its secret level.

Lastly, the game itself has a bit of a bad GUI design. Sometimes game element simply are invisible because the healthbar, or one of the other big items are drawn over it. It would've been great to have a button to either make the GUI smaller, or hide completely. Alternatively, the levels should be bigger so that you can scroll more up/down and simply see what's normally under the GUI controls.

I had such a difficult time solving one puzzle, because one of the necessary pylons was completely hidden due to the health bar. I just guessed that it had to be there after 30 minutes of scratching my head and solved the puzzle afterwards.

There is a ? button that explains how the game works. I advise you to click it and browse through all pages. It allowed me to learn many of the keyboard shortcuts which made the game more playable.

Overall, this is a good game. It just has a few minor problems with it. If the dev's would fix these, it would turn a good game into a great game for sure.

But the game is free anyway and because of that, I can definitely recommend this game to anyone who likes puzzles.

So, try it. If you don't like it, just delete the game. Its free.
